LinSCP {version} - secure file transfer:
LinSCP {version} - secure file transfer client

  linscp [options] [sftp://[user[:password]@]host[:port]/[path]]

Options:
  -script=FILE      execute commands from FILE ('-' reads stdin)
  -command=CMD      execute commands (separate several with ';')
  -literal          with -command, treat %...% in paths as literal text
  -rawsettings[=N]  session defaults as N NAME=VALUE arguments (also -shell)
  -hostkey=KEY      pin the host key (fingerprint or '*' for this connection)
  -password=PWD     password to use (prefer the LINSCP_PASSWORD variable)
  -privatekey=FILE  OpenSSH/PEM or PPK v2/v3 private key for authentication
  -passphrase=PWD   private-key passphrase (avoid exposing it in process lists)
  -convertkey=FILE  convert a PPK v2/v3 key (requires -output=FILE)
  -output=FILE      destination PEM file for -convertkey (no overwrite)
  -username=NAME    user name to authenticate with
  -port=NUMBER      port to connect to (default 22)
  -timeout=SECS     connection timeout in seconds (default 15)
  -clientcert=FILE  TLS client certificate for FTPS and WebDAVS
  -implicit[=on|off] / -explicit[=ON|OFF]  the TLS mode of an FTP session
  -passive[=on|off] choose the FTP data connection policy
  -log=FILE         log the session to FILE
  -loglevel=LEVEL   logging level: -1 reduced, 0 normal, 1 debug, 2 debug2
  -logsize=[N*]SIZE rotate the log at SIZE bytes, keeping N older files
  -xmllog=FILE      write an XML log of every command and operation to
                    FILE (upstream session format; passwords masked)
  -batch            never ask, abort instead
  -parameter VAL..  script parameters, for %1% .. %9%, %TIMESTAMP% and
                    %ENVIRONMENT% expansion in the commands
  -gui              launch the graphical Commander desktop interface
  -shell            open an interactive shell on the site given as
                    the argument; stdin and stdout are the raw byte
                    pipe of the shell, as the graphical client's
                    embedded terminal uses it
  -server           command server of the graphical client: one command
                    per line on stdin, 'LSCP-RESULT <code>' after each
  -verbose          print SSH event log messages
  -version          print the version and exit
  -help             print this help and exit

Commands:
  open SITE         connect to a site (sftp://user@host:port/path)
  close [INDEX]     disconnect the open session, or session INDEX
  cd DIR            change the remote directory
  pwd               print the remote directory
  ls [-al1] [DIR]   list remote files
  versions [OBJECT] list S3 object versions and delete markers
  lcd DIR           change the local directory
  lpwd              print the local directory
  lls [DIR[/MASK]]  list local files with date, time and size
  get [opts] REMOTE [LOCAL]  download file(s) or directories
  put [opts] LOCAL [REMOTE]  upload file(s) or directories
                    both: -r -delete -neweronly -resume -append -preservetime
                    -speed=KB -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic -filemask=MASK
                    -resumesupport=on|off|KB -rawtransfersettings[=N]
                    -permissions[=OCTAL] -nopermissions
                    -versionid=ID (S3 get/rm; versions lists history)
  synchronize local|remote|both [LOCAL [REMOTE]] [switches]
                    synchronize directories: -delete -preview
                    -nonrecursive -filemask=MASK
                    -criteria=time|size|checksum|either|both|none
  keepuptodate [LOCAL [REMOTE]] [switches]
                    reflect local changes on the remote side; the local
                    tree is watched, -interval=SECS polls instead
                    (-count=N bounds the passes; Ctrl-C stops watching)
  edit FILE         edit a remote file in an external editor
                    (-force, -keep, -editor=COMMAND)
  session [INDEX]   list the open sessions, or switch to INDEX
  sessions [NAME]   list stored sites; NAME opens one, and
                    (also: sessions export FILE, sessions import FILE)
  savesession NAME  store the current connection as a named session
                    (-preset=NAME stores its transfer preset)
  rmsession NAME    forget a stored session
  presets           list the transfer presets; savepreset NAME K=V...
                    stores one, rmspreset NAME removes one
  rm FILE           remove remote file(s)
  rmdir DIR         remove a remote directory
  mkdir [-parents] DIR  create a remote directory (parents if requested)
  mv FROM TO        move/rename a remote file
  chmod MODE FILE [FILE...] [-recursive]
                    change remote permissions; MODE is octal (644) or
                    symbolic (u+x, a=r,go-w)
  copyid [KEYFILE]  add the public key of KEYFILE, or of the session key,
                    to the server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
  stat FILE         print the listing line of a remote path
  attr FILE         print remote file attributes, key/value
  terminal          open an interactive shell on the server
  echo [MESSAGE]    display text message
  option confirm|batch|resume|editor|editmaxsize|transfer|preset VALUE
                    configure session options (preset NAME makes a
                    transfer preset the default, 'option preset off' clears)
  binary / ascii    select the transfer mode of the following commands
  help              list the commands (alias: man)
  exit              end the session

  Records an ETag precondition for one WebDAV path with this

  sends it in the If header next to any lock token, so the
  server refuses (412) a write over a version this client has

  '-clear' forgets the precondition. Give exactly one of the

open <site> [-hostkey=KEY] [-password=PW:
open <site> [-hostkey=KEY] [-password=PWD] [-username=NAME]
        [-privatekey=FILE] [-passphrase=PHR] [-clientcert=FILE]
        [-timeout=SEC] [-implicit[=on|off]] [-explicit[=on|off]]
        [-passive[=on|off]] [-sessionname=NAME]
        [-rawsettings NAME=VALUE...]
  Connects to a site given as a URL or a stored session name;
  the switches apply to a stored site as well as to a URL.
  -timeout is the server response timeout in seconds.
  -implicit and -explicit choose the TLS mode of an FTP
  session (implicit TLS uses port 990 when the URL names no
  port); -passive turns the FTP data connection policy on or
  off; -clientcert is the TLS client certificate file;
  -sessionname is the name this connection is logged under.
  -rawsettings sets session settings by upstream's names. This
  build applies the proxy ones (ProxyMethod=None|SOCKS4|SOCKS5|
  HTTP|Telnet|Cmd, ProxyHost, ProxyPort, ProxyUsername,
  ProxyPassword, ProxyTelnetCommand, ProxyLocalCommand,
  ProxyDNS=0|1|2, ProxyLocalhost=0|1, ProxyExcludeList), the FTP
  engine's policy (FtpPasvMode=0|1, FtpForcePasvIp=0|1|2,
  FtpUseMlsd=0|1|2, FtpAccount) and the TLS policy (Ftps=0|1|2|3,
  MinTlsVersion, MaxTlsVersion, TlsCertificateFile,
  TlsCertificateKeyFile, CaCertificateFile, CaCertificateDir,
  PinnedPublicKey); any other setting is refused rather than
  dropped.
option [ <name> [ <value> ] ]\n Shows o:
option [ <name> [ <value> ] ]
  Shows or changes a setting: echo, batch, confirm, resume,
  transfer, include, exclude, failonnomatch, synchdelete,
  reconnecttime, editor, editmaxsize, preset. Without a name it
  prints every setting; a name or a value may be abbreviated
  as long as the abbreviation is unambiguous.
presets\n Lists the transfer presets fr:
presets
  Lists the transfer presets from the user configuration.
  A preset is stored with 'savepreset <name> <setting>...'
  (transfer=binary|ascii|automatic, preservetime=on|off|all,
  neweronly, speed=<KB/s>, resumesupport=on|off|<KB>,
  permissions=<octal>|off|fromfile, host=, user=, remotedir=,
  localdir=, mask=); 'rmspreset <name>' removes one.
  'option preset <name>' makes a preset the default for the
  following transfer commands, 'option preset off' disables
  presets for this session (even matching rules); a stored
  site loads its own when it is opened.

property <file> -get=NAME | property <file> -set=NAME=VALUE
  Reads or writes one WebDAV dead property of a file, in this
  client's own namespace. '-get' prints 'NAME is not set' when
  the server says the property does not exist.
put [ <switches> ] <file> [ <file>... ]:
put [ <switches> ] <file> [ <file>... ] [ <target> ]
  Uploads files; the switches of 'get' (on uploads,
  -permissions without a value keeps the local file's own
  mode on the server); -append adds to the remote file
  instead of replacing it (native SFTP only, and not
  together with -resume); -latest uploads only the newest
  local file the command named.

rmspreset <name>\n Removes the transfer:
rmspreset <name>
  Removes the transfer preset <name>; if it was active,
  transfers go back to their own settings.
savepreset <name> <setting>[=<value>]...
  Stores or updates a transfer preset; settings without a
  value (neweronly) are switches. See 'help presets'.
savesession <name> [ options ]\n Stores:
savesession <name> [ options ]
  Stores the current session, or the one the options
  describe, under <name>; -preset=NAME also stores the
  transfer preset the site should load (-preset= clears it),
  and -rawsettings NAME=VALUE... stores session settings with
  it (the ones 'open -rawsettings' applies: proxy, FTP engine
  and TLS policy; a proxy password is encrypted like a session
  password).

sessions [ NAME | list | export <file> | import <file> ]
  Lists the stored sites, opens one by name, or exports and
  imports the whole list.

show

synchronize local|remote|both [ <localdi:
synchronize local|remote|both [ <localdir> [ <remotedir> ] ]
  [ -delete ] [-nodelete] [-mirror] [-preview]
  [-criteria=time|size|checksum|either|both|none] [-filemask=<mask>]
  [-transfer=binary|ascii|automatic] [-nonrecursive]
  The criteria say what counts as a change: 'time' (the
  default) copies a file the source has newer, 'size' one of
  a different size, 'checksum' one whose contents differ and
  'none' every file. 'either' and its synonym 'both' compare
  the time and the size, and the three comparisons may also
  be listed, as in -criteria=time,checksum. In the 'both'
  direction the record of the previous synchronization
  decides, so 'checksum' and 'none' are refused there.

terminal

versions [ <object-or-prefix> ]
  Lists S3 object versions and delete markers. An object path
  lists that exact key; a bucket or trailing-slash prefix
  lists every matching key. Results are paginated.
